slides.headline:
Korea's biggest food
holiday starts Thursday.
slides.subline: Chuseok runs 24–26 September. The palaces open free and the expressways go toll-free — and a lot of the restaurants you bookmarked pull the shutters down

slides.label: Chuseok 2026 runs Thursday 24 to Saturday 26 September, with Chuseok Day itself on Friday the 25th. Monday the 28th is a normal working day
slides.note: Sources: Seoul Economic Daily, 13 Sep 2026 — the three-day holiday, and that the government is not officially reviewing a temporary holiday for 28 Sep · Korea Tourism Organization (VisitKorea) official 2026 Chuseok travel guide · Checked 19 September 2026

items.t: Four palaces and Jongmyo, no ticket
items.d: Gyeongbokgung, Changdeokgung, Changgyeonggung and Deoksugung, plus Jongmyo Shrine and the Joseon royal tombs. Changdeokgung's rear garden stays excluded
It normally requires an advance reservation. Over the holiday the Korea Times reports visitors can enter without one
Nationwide, from midnight on the 24th to midnight on the 27th. Some regions are waiving tolls on privately financed roads and bridges too
Guard-changing at 10am and 2pm, guard patrols at 11am and 1pm, and a royal guard patrol at 3pm

slides.title:
But the food
goes quiet.
slides.body:
Chuseok is a harvest holiday, and the cooking that defines it happens in homes rather than restaurants. Songpyeon — half-moon rice cakes steamed over a bed of pine needles — is made at the kitchen table, alongside jeon, japchae and yakgwa.

Korea's own tourism office is direct about the consequence: department stores and many restaurants close on Chuseok Day, while convenience stores and shops near tourist attractions usually stay open. Subways and city buses run normally. It says holiday hours vary enough that you should check each venue's website before going.

So treat Friday the 25th as the day to plan around, and keep the independent places you bookmarked for either side of it.

items.t: The 25th is the worst day to drive
items.d: TMAP and SK Telecom forecast Seoul to Busan at 7 hours 3 minutes leaving at noon on the 25th, and 8 hours coming back the same day — roughly 2.5 hours over normal

items.t: KTX and SRT are one system now
items.d: They merged on 1 September 2026. The old SRT app no longer books — use KORAIL+. Fares on existing KTX routes were cut about 10 percent to match SRT pricing
The tourism office warns train and express bus tickets sell out quickly as demand surges over major holidays. If you haven't booked, plan around staying put
The Korea Travel Hotline, run by the Korea Tourism Organization, is the number to call when you need to find something that's actually open

slides.text:
This is research, not a personal visit.
Every fact here comes from a published source, checked on 19 September 2026.
slides.by:
Two things are not fully settled. The Korea Times describes the palace free-entry window as Thursday through Sunday, while the tourism office frames the holiday itself as Thursday to Saturday — so treat Sunday the 27th as likely but worth checking.
And Monday the 28th was still a normal working day as of 13 September, with no temporary holiday under official review. If that changes, closures shift with it.

caption:
Chuseok 2026 falls on Friday 25 September, with the holiday running Thursday 24 to Saturday 26. If you're in Korea that week, it changes what you can eat and where you can go.

What opens up: Gyeongbokgung, Changdeokgung, Changgyeonggung and Deoksugung are free, along with Jongmyo Shrine and the Joseon royal tombs — and Jongmyo waives its usual advance-booking rule. Expressway tolls are waived nationwide from midnight on the 24th to midnight on the 27th.

What closes: department stores and many restaurants shut on Chuseok Day itself, and independent owner-run places often stay closed longer than the three official days. Convenience stores and shops near tourist attractions generally stay open, and subways and city buses run normally.

Two things worth knowing before you move: TMAP forecasts Seoul to Busan at seven hours leaving at noon on the 25th, and KTX and SRT merged on 1 September — the old SRT app no longer books tickets, so use KORAIL+.

The food of the holiday is songpyeon, half-moon rice cakes steamed over pine needles, made at home rather than sold in restaurants.

Sources in the last slide. Save it before the 24th.
